Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1226 PM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE NORTHEAST...NORTHWEST NEBRASKA INTO SOUTH-CENTRAL SOUTH
DAKOTA...NORTHWEST OKLAHOMA INTO SOUTHWEST MISSOURI...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over small parts of the Great Plains,
and over the Northeast on Thursday with locally strong wind gusts.
Isolated hail may occur with the Northern Plains/Ozarks activity.

...Northwest Oklahoma into southwest Missouri...
A stalled surface boundary is expected to be draped across southern
Kansas into central Missouri. The Missouri portion of the boundary
will likely be reinforced by early day convection/cloud cover.
Strong heating south of the boundary will allow for locally enhanced
surface convergence. Storm development is possible along the
boundary, though it remains uncertain where this development is most
probable. The presence of the broad trough to the north will support
sufficient shear that storms would be at least marginally organized.
Damaging wind gusts will likely be the main threat with this
activity with marginal hail possible where buoyancy will be locally
greater in Missouri.

...Northeast...
Areas of modest to strong heating of a very moist (70+ F dewpoints)
airmass will support 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE by mid-afternoon.
Deep-layer shear will not be overly strong, but enhanced mid-level
winds associated with the Great Lakes trough will promote marginally
organized clusters/linear segments. Isolated wind damage will be
possible with this activity.

...Nebraska/South Dakota...
A secondary cold front will develop within the northern Plains.
Moisture return ahead of the boundary will bring upper 50s to low
60s F dewpoint northward. Mid-level heights are forecast to rise
slightly during the period. Given effective shear of around 40 kt
across the boundary, an isolated supercell or two will be possible
where surface heating can remove MLCIN. Severe winds and marginally
severe hail would be the expected hazards. The Marginal risk remains
where confidence in storm development is highest, though a storm or
two could develop farther northeast. Confidence remains too low for
an expansion of probabilities.

..Wendt.. 08/05/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0234 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong storms may occur over parts of the Northeast and Upper
Mississippi Valley region on Friday. Locally strong wind gusts
appear most likely.

...Northeast...
Beneath modest southwest winds aloft, a large area of thunderstorms
is likely Friday afternoon from the TN Valley/Appalachians into the
Northeast, as daytime heating combines with a moist air mass and
marginal instability. General thunderstorm activity appears most
likely across these areas given weak winds at or below 20 kt below
700 mb. However, increasing daytime storm coverage could produce
locally gusty winds/outflows, especially where pockets of greater
instability develop with the higher dewpoints over eastern areas.

...WI/MN/IA...
A northwest flow regime over the northern Plains will gradually move
toward the Upper Great Lakes Friday into Saturday, with cooling
temperatures aloft and 500 mb winds on the order of 30-35 kt. A weak
surface trough may develop from Lake Superior southwestward into IA
during the day, with eventual destabilization as southwest winds at
850 mb increase to around 20 kt. Shear will not be particularly
strong, but storms are likely late in the day into the overnight
from WI into IA. While isolated severe gusts or hail cannot be ruled
out, predictability issues preclude adding a risk area at this time.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0400 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 081200Z - 131200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Saturday/D4...
Southwest midlevel winds of only 25 kt will exist across the
Northeast, while low-level moisture remains in place supporting up
to 2000 J/kg MUCAPE with poor lapse rates aloft. This will support
daytime thunderstorms over a large area from the Appalachians into
the Northeast, and a few severe gusts cannot be ruled out.
Otherwise, normal gusty outflow winds are to be expected.

To the west, an area of stronger instability is forecast across the
Mid MO Valley, where northwesterly midlevel winds of 35 kt will
exist along the southern periphery of a trough sweeping across the
Upper Great Lakes. Evening/overnight storms may occur across parts
of eastern NE, IA, and MO, and instability may be large enough to
warrant at least low severe probabilities as the event nears in
time.

...Sunday/D5...
Drying will occur aloft over parts of the Northeast as a wave moves
into Quebec, but substantial low-level moisture will still support
scattered thunderstorms ahead of a cold front across the Mid
Atlantic. Shear will again be weak, but perhaps enough mean wind
speeds will exist for storms to be mobile/produce areas of strong
gusts.

To the west, low-level moisture is forecast to shift a bit farther
north into the Dakotas, and this will occur beneath stronger
northwest flow aloft. This area bears watching in later outlooks, as
wind profiles may somewhat favor supercells. Predictability is
currently low.

...Mon/D6 to Wed/D8...
While predictability decreases further during this time frame,
moderate west to northwest flow aloft will remain from the upper MS
Valley across the Great Lakes, which will spread into the Northeast
D7/D8. If a wave does amplify within this flow regime, a corridor of
damaging winds could develop given upper 60s to low 70s F dewpoints
along/south of the mean frontal zone (roughly IA to NY/PA by end of
the period). Model variation is currently too great to depict an
precise corridor.

..Jewell.. 08/05/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1130 AM CDT Wed Aug 05 2026

Valid 051630Z - 061200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...ARIZONA...AND
THE SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible today and tonight across
eastern Kansas into the mid Mississippi Valley. Isolated severe
gusts and hail may also occur across parts of the southern High
Plains and Arizona.

...Eastern Kansas into the Mid Mississippi Valley...
Severe potential this afternoon through tonight will be complicated
by ongoing convection/precipitation from eastern KS into the mid MS
Valley. In general, filtered daytime heating will occur along/ahead
of a surface front across these regions through the afternoon, with
this area on the southern periphery of mid/upper-level troughing
over central Canada and the northern Plains/Upper Midwest. An
embedded mid-level disturbance is aiding the ongoing sub-severe
convection. Current expectations are for at least isolated strong to
severe thunderstorms to develop later this afternoon and evening in
the gradually destabilizing airmass, with sufficient deep-layer
shear forecast to support some updraft organization. Occasional hail
and damaging winds may occur with the stronger cores, but evolution
into one or more bowing clusters remains uncertain. A stronger
signal exists for scattered to numerous thunderstorms to develop
late this evening into early Thursday morning across eastern KS into
MO in a strengthening low-level warm advection regime, with a
continued severe hail/wind threat possible given ample MUCAPE and
strong shear forecast in the cloud-bearing layer.

...Arizona...
A seasonably moist low-level airmass (with surface observations
generally in the low to mid 60s) will undergo further heating
through late afternoon. Orographic lift should favor convection
developing over the higher terrain and gradually spreading into the
lower deserts this evening, as modest mid-level easterly flow
persists to the south of upper ridging centered over the Southwest.
Very steep low to mid-level lapse rates will contribute to a risk
for strong downdrafts capable of producing at least isolated severe
gusts (60-80 mph). Considered adding a Slight Risk based on
scattered thunderstorm coverage moving into the lower deserts. But,
given ongoing cloud cover across parts of central/southeast AZ and a
tendency for the mid-level easterly flow to gradually weaken through
the evening, confidence in scattered severe gusts occurring remains
too low for an upgrade at this time.

...Southern High Plains...
Weak post-frontal low-level upslope flow into the Raton Mesa
vicinity will favor widely scattered convective development across
the southern High Plains by mid to late afternoon. Modest
west-northwesterly mid-level flow will favor motions to the
east-southeast into the adjacent High Plains along/near a surface
cold front. With steep lapse rates and a relatively dry sub-cloud
layer expected, evaporative cooling will probably result in a few
storms being capable of isolated severe gusts. A gust of 75+ mph may
occur given the very well mixed boundary layer. Isolated, marginally
severe hail may also occur with the initial cells that develop.

..Gleason/Lyons.. 08/05/2026
